title: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH
request: The installer currently completes while the launcher directory never reaches PATH in a freshly opened terminal. It picks the profile file from $SHELL alone: on macOS a bash login shell never reads ~/.bashrc, and under `curl … | sh` $SHELL can be empty, sending the block to ~/.profile while the terminal reads ~/.zshrc. It also never checks that its own change took effect. This change makes the installer detect the real login shell, write the block into a profile file a new terminal actually reads, start a clean login shell afterwards and verify that `forgel-code` resolves, and fail with a message naming the edited file and the observed PATH when it does not. --uninstall removes the block from every profile file the installer can have written.

audit.summary: The release implements most of the PATH detection, guarded block, fresh-shell verification and uninstall work, and the suite passes, but blocking defects remain. The fresh-shell watchdog creates predictable world-readable files under /tmp, ignores its timeout status when deciding success, and can still hang on a shell that ignores SIGTERM. Re-installing over a pre-existing profile also accumulates the separator blank line, so the profile is not byte-identical across runs.

findings.issue: `bounded_run` creates its state files at predictable paths `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/forgel-code-check.$$.{out,done,killed}` and initializes them with `: >` instead of a private `mktemp` file. A local user can pre-create a symlink for a guessed PID and cause the installer to truncate an arbitrary file writable by the installing user. The redirected fresh-shell output is also created with the default umask and may be readable by other users.
findings.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with `mktemp -d` (mode 0700), create files with mode 0600, clean up the directory, and avoid following pre-existing symlinks.

findings.issue: `verify_profile` ignores `BOUNDED_STATUS`. `bounded_run` sets it to 124 when the watchdog kills the shell, but if the captured output already contains `forgel-fresh-resolved=<launcher>`, `verify_profile` returns success. In addition, the watchdog only sends SIGTERM and the parent then blocks in `wait "$child"`, so a shell that ignores SIGTERM defeats the bounded time limit. The watchdog test only covers a shell that prints nothing and dies on TERM.
findings.suggestion: Treat `BOUNDED_STATUS=124` as a verification failure regardless of captured output, escalate from SIGTERM to SIGKILL after a grace period, and add a test where the detected shell prints the expected resolution and then hangs or ignores TERM.

findings.issue: Re-install idempotence is not preserved for a profile that already contains user content. `add_profile_block` appends a blank line before the block whenever the file is non-empty, while the unchanged `remove_profile_block` is documented to keep every other line. Each re-run therefore leaves an additional separator blank line, violating the requirement that the rest of the file stay byte-identical. The new idempotence tests only cover an initially empty profile.
findings.suggestion: Remove the installer-added separator along with the marked block, or avoid adding a new separator when the preceding content already ends with a blank line. Add a test that seeds the profile with user content, runs install twice, and asserts exact bytes.

findings.issue: `detect_login_shell` accepts `$SHELL` when its basename is handled, but `verify_profile` only starts it when `[ -x "$shell" ]`. A valid `SHELL=zsh` (a bare command name) is detected, the block is written, then verification is skipped and the install exits non-zero even though `zsh` is available on PATH.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the selected shell with `command -v` before the `-x` check, or return the resolved executable path from detection. Add a test with a bare `$SHELL` name.

findings.issue: `CHANGELOG.md` says `--uninstall` cleans the override profile in addition to the "six standard profile files", but `install.sh` and `README.md` now clean seven standard files including `~/.bashrc`.
findings.suggestion: Update the changelog entry to say seven standard profile files, or list the files explicitly.

detail: The release audit for `code` returned verdict `fail` with one critical and two major findings that are real defects in `install.sh` itself, not in the specification: the request explicitly requires bounded verification that fails with a message naming the edited file and observed PATH, and requires that a re-install leave the rest of the profile byte-identical. The earlier attempt to route this back never queued a task, so the code is still unchanged and the release cannot be accepted or published as-is.
